description: Wavetable oscillator with a built-in editor — up to 256 wave cycles of 2048 samples, drawn partial by partial, imported from a file or a picture, or sampled from the input

params.text: Switches the sync input between soft sync, which turns the cycle round, and hard sync, which restarts it
Sets the pitch in semitones, 0 giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Trims the pitch a semitone either way
Sets how deeply the FM jack moves the frequency, from none to full
Chooses which wave cycle is being edited, across however many the wavetable holds
Chooses which wave cycle is played, across however many the wavetable holds
Attenuverts the voltage that moves the played cycle, -1 to +1
Sets how many slightly detuned copies of the oscillator sound at once, 1 to 3
Sets how far apart in pitch those copies are detuned
Records the signal at the input into the whole wavetable, filling it cycle by cycle
Records the signal at the input into the cycle being edited
Turns the three-dimensional view of the whole wavetable on and off
Opens a wav file and splits it into wave cycles across the wavetable
Opens a wav file and writes it into the cycle being edited
Opens a png file and builds a wavetable from the contrast in the picture
Fills the empty cycles between the ones already there by fading between their samples
Fills the empty cycles between the ones already there by fading between the strength and the phase of each partial
Fills the empty cycles between the ones already there by fading between the strength of each partial, holding the phase of the first cycle throughout
Throws away every cycle that was filled in by a morph, leaving the ones loaded or drawn
Scales every cycle by one gain, taken from the loudest point anywhere in the wavetable, so the relative levels between cycles are kept
Scales the cycle being edited up to full level
Scales every cycle up to full level on its own, which flattens the differences between them
Takes the constant offset out of every cycle
Fades every cycle in and out with a Blackman-Harris window, which kills the click of a cycle that does not meet itself at the ends
Fades the cycle being edited in and out with a Blackman-Harris window
Averages the samples at the two ends of every cycle so they meet
Averages the samples at the two ends of the cycle being edited so they meet
Adds an empty cycle to the wavetable
Removes the cycle being edited from the wavetable
Turns the drawing of the cycle being edited on and off
Turns the drawing of the cycle being played on and off

inputs.text: Pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob
Modulates the frequency, scaled by the FM knob
A rising edge here syncs the oscillator
A trigger here switches the sync between soft and hard
Moves through the wave cycles, scaled by the attenuverter beside it, which is what sweeps the wavetable
The signal that is sampled into the wavetable or into a single cycle
Adds to the detuning between the unison copies

notes: the wavetable is empty when the module is loaded and the oscillator is silent until something is put in it: load a wav or aiff file, build one from a png, or record one from the input
a wav or aiff file dropped onto the panel is cut into cycles across the whole wavetable
drag up and down on the upper graph to set the strength of one partial of the cycle being edited, and on the lower graph to set its phase
hold the control key while dragging on either graph of the display to take that partial to zero
menu: Wavetable display: — turns the three-dimensional drawing of the whole wavetable on and off
Edited frame display: — turns the drawing of the cycle being edited on and off
Played frame display: — turns the drawing of the cycle being played on and off
Save wavetable as wav — writes the whole wavetable out as a wav file
Save frame as wav — writes the cycle being edited out as a wav file
Save wavetable as png — writes the whole wavetable out as a png picture
